name: Solve a Rubik’s Cube one-handed
blurb: The same method with half the hands. It requires re-learning your algorithms as one-handed finger tricks and using the table for the moves you cannot do.
steps: Get comfortable solving two-handed without thinking first — one-handed adds a physical problem to an already busy mental one.
Loosen the cube’s tension. One-handed solving needs a much easier turn than two-handed.
Learn one-handed U turns with the index finger and thumb, which is the foundation of everything.
Learn to rotate the whole cube in one hand without dropping it.
Re-learn your algorithms as one-handed sequences, using table abuse — pressing the cube against the table — for awkward turns.
Practise both hands if you are ambitious, and time yourself to track progress.
tips: A tight cube makes this miserable. Loosen it and use lube.
Practise over a table or a bed. You will drop it hundreds of times.
proof: A full solve one-handed, under two minutes, without dropping the cube.
